description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:1005 calls pkix_path::validate_path(&chain, anchors, policy, verifier) once per yielded candidate. validate_path re-runs all of: check_inputs, check_oid_consistency, anchor matching (anchor DN compared against last cert's issuer), path-length check, AND then the full signature chain walk. For a pool that yields N candidate chains with M anchors, anchor matching alone is O(N*M) name_match calls; the input guards repeat for every candidate. For typical pools (3-5 candidates, 1-100 anchors) this is fine. For adversarial pools that yield many candidates against a large anchor store (Mozilla bundle ~150 anchors), this is significant. Optimization opportunity: identify the anchor index once at the start of build_first_valid_path (anchors[i] whose subject_dn matches the deepest cert's issuer), then either pass it to validate_path via a variant or factor anchor matching out. Not blocking for 1.0 — flag for awareness. The shape of build_first_valid_path's current API doesn't admit anchor-pinning without a new entry point, so this is a forward-looking efficiency note.
title: build_first_valid_path re-runs validate_path's input guards per-candidate; large anchor sets pay O(candidates * anchors)
